name: Reed Miller
desc: Avrelian was the ideal heir who was supposed to lead the Frosmoon Scions to the Elysium. He was the Great Thief, Reed Miller, and the founder of the Treasure Hoarders. Avrelian lived 500 years ago.

imgDesc.text: Avrelian and Solovei in their youth.

customize.name: Frostmoon Scions
customize.desc: The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning all civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess."

customize.text:
Avrelian was the ideal heir, destined to lead the Frostmoon Scions to the Elysium. His mother ran away with an officer from Snezhnaya, but was later captured by the priestess Lovia and Rotwang. The officer was killed, and the girl committed suicide. She hoped Avrelian would never return to Nod-Krai.
Mikhnenko
After Avrelian's parents died, he was adopted by a rank-and-file military officer named Mikhnenko. As a result, he was able to attend the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy.

customize.name: Nod-Krai
customize.desc:
The moon-blessed land located in the northwestern regions of Teyvat.

Follow the silver thread spun by the new moon, traverse biting gales and desolate tundras as the snow-kissed lakes, fractured like mirrors, reflect their ageless, glacial radiance. The days are bitterly short, and the night stretches on like a dark, yawning maw. But even then, the light and song of the Welkin Moon will dance gently across the faces of visiting travelers. Up at ye towers, and let your lanterns blaze into the darkness! Until the day comes... when true moonlight bathes this land once more.

customize.text: Shortly after Avrelian became a non-commissioned officer, he "died in the line of duty" for unknown reasons. He surfaced in Nod-Krai a few years later under the name Reed Miller, gathering the destitute who lived on the fringes of society into a band that became the first Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Alia
customize.desc: The second Reed Miller and the First Moonchanter's sister from the Frostmoon Scions. She lived 500 years ago.

customize.text:
The second Reed Miller after Avrelian's death. She molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own. Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night.
Brahe
The adoptive son of the fae lord Trubetskoy, governor of all Nod-Krai, and the third Reed Miller. One day, he saw Alia robbing the governor's palace and fell in love with her. He abandoned his noble life to join the Treasure Hoarders. Brahe invented legends about Reed Miller's treasure, romanticizing the story of the Great Thief.

customize.name: Dawning Frost
customize.desc: A silver-forged ritual vessel, pure and completely without blemish. It is said to be a sacred relic passed down for generations among the priestesses of the far north.

customize.name: The First Iron Coin
customize.desc:
An aged iron coin engraved with a stylized raven sigil. Legend says it was forged by Reed Miller, founder of the Treasure Hoarders, and was the very first true "Iron Coin."
In a world without borders, in a paradise where no one suffers from hunger or cold, the gold bestowed and governed by the Deus Auri was never meant to serve as the foundation of human cooperation.
Humans should be masters of money, not its servants. Even if one cannot claim the heart of gold for themselves, all should be able to wield the wealth that inherently belongs to everyone.

But that is a story of a much later time. Whether it was the first iron coin or the ideals sung, interpreted, and twisted over the following centuries,
it all began on a winter night beyond the reach of lamplight, when two children slipped out of the academy, hiding from the adults' eyes, and carved a token for playing the Thief Extraordinaire.

customize.name: The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire
Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather
customize.desc: A feather as dark as night. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication
customize.desc: A goblet lavishly adorned. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask
customize.desc: A cold mask that once concealed a true face. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders. No adornments grace the mask but for the frosty moonlight that dances across its pure silver facade.

customize.name: Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest
customize.desc: An artificial flower stained with rust. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow
customize.desc: A timepiece long since stopped. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Treasure Hoarder Insignia
customize.desc: A signet that proudly represents its owner's position as member of the Treasure Hoarders. The pursuit of treasure knows no bounds. That said... Is being a thief something to be proud of?

customize.name: Silver Raven Insignia
customize.desc: A raven insignia used by members of the Treasure Hoarders to identify each other. The Treasure Hoarders ask for no resume. Anyone who has an insatiable desire for treasure and is backed up by an equal amount of courage can become a worthy member.

customize.name: Golden Raven Insignia
customize.desc: A raven insignia that symbolizes the pride and the guiding principle of the Treasure Hoarders. Whether it's hidden amidst the vastness of the land or in the depths of the seas, as long as there are treasures to be hunted down, the spirit of Treasure Hoarders, who will stop at nothing to acquire them, will never die.

customize.name: Teachings of Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
There are those who are desperate to get in, and those who are desperate to get out. Perhaps Elysium is not a place one can ever truly reach.

customize.name: Guide to Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
To create a paradise without borders or distinctions upon a land overflowing with bitterness and sorrow — though it might be but a childish delusion, it may yet be a foundation for the future.

customize.name: Philosophies of Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
Seldom do we share the same dreams of paradise. For those who wish not to settle for the present, there is no greater paradise than Nod-Krai. Yet for all the rest, the truth is quite the opposite.

customize.name: Artful Device Fragment
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
An intricate device once known as the "Seven Tools of the Great Thief." Rumors claim it was created by the legendary thief, Reed Miller.
Just as the first Treasure Hoarders came from all walks of life, this combination of tools meant for different purposes was designed to break down artificial boundaries, regardless of whether they were chains or borders.
It should be noted that there are more than seven tools, its just that people are accustomed to using seven to describe anything numerous. Perhaps it is for the same reason that the world is believed to have only seven forms of order.

customize.name: Artful Device Replica
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Just as the legendary thief's tools have been imitated by countless others, so has his name.
In a sense, it was not the people who thirsted for something more who stole Reed Miller's name, but rather Reed Miller who stole the identity that was originally theirs alone. These viewpoints are just two sides of the same coin.

customize.name: Artful Device Inheritance
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Word on the street is that the legendary thief, Reed Miller, has been sentenced to death several times, yet he's always managed to escape at the last minute with the help of his friends — and his tools.
In some versions of these stories, several of his followers willingly died in his place for their revered King of Elysium. Naturally, these versions can't compete with the more popular drunken stories full of romance and bliss. Since there has never been a shackle that could restrain the legendary thief, it is only natural to assume that no ending could do the same.

customize.name: Artful Device Wish
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
"The poor, the starving, the wretched, the oppressed! My exiled brothers and sisters!"
"If you, too, have tasted indignities at the cruel hands of fate! If you, too, have wept in the night at the plight of your neighbors!"
"If you, too, have longed for a shelter from fear! If you, too, have dreamed of a world where no tears are shed!"
"Then join us, your brothers and sisters, in breaking the chains of slavery!"
"Let the dead bury the dead, for you will rise up, and with the treasures of the haughty, we will build an Elysium without boundaries!"
